topic: How a capacitor charges through a resistor (the RC time constant)

segments.narration: Why does a camera flash need a moment before it fires?
segments.visual: Title 'Charging a Capacitor' with subtitle 'the RC circuit'

segments.narration: Inside is a capacitor charging through a resistor. Connect a battery, and current begins to flow into the capacitor.
segments.visual: A simple circuit loop: battery V0 on the left, resistor R on top, capacitor C on the right

segments.narration: The capacitor's voltage climbs quickly at first, then slows down as it fills up.
segments.visual: Axes below the circuit, with the charging curve drawn from left to right

segments.narration: The curve is V naught times one minus e to the minus t over R C.
segments.visual: The equation V(t) = V0 (1 - e^(-t/RC)) below the axes

segments.narration: R times C is called tau, the time constant, measured in seconds.
segments.visual: A dashed vertical line at t = tau on the axes, labelled tau = RC

segments.narration: After one tau, the capacitor sits at about sixty three percent of full charge.
segments.visual: A dashed horizontal line at 63 percent meeting the curve at tau

segments.narration: By five tau it is essentially full. A bigger resistor or capacitor stretches the curve, charging slower.
segments.visual: A dot at five tau near the top of the curve, and the payoff 'tau = RC sets the speed'
